verses.verse:
यदा छिद्रस्य संकोचः स्थात्तदा नादनीचता।
यदा छिद्रस्य विस्तारस्तदा स्याद् विपरीतता।।२६।।
verses.text: When a hole is narrowed, the sound becomes lower; when a hole is widened, the reverse.

commentary.text: That is, in the distances between the holes of Dha, Ni, Ni and Sa there is so fine an unevenness that it is hard to solve by gaṇita (calculation). So the fault can be removed simply by making the komal Ni hole slightly smaller than the Dha hole. The proof of this can only be the attentive ear of musicians. So the meaning of the above śloka is: if the hole is narrowed, the sound becomes lower than its place, and if the hole is made bigger, the sound becomes higher than its place, that is its śruti. But this raising and lowering of the sound will be limited to four śrutis at most. Taking advantage of this procedure, we can also gain ease in the rakhāv (placement) of the fingers.
